tips.li: Goods for a mission must be in a stockpile or on a shelf, unforbidden, to count. Something a cook has already claimed doesn't.
A mission that fails costs the goodwill it would have earned, and the people who asked remember it.
When the goods won't be ready in time, a caravan to a trader may still buy what's missing.
A world event changes what comes to the colony while it lasts: plague in the region makes illness at home likelier, a famine brings the hungry to the gate.
Caravans come less often while the region is in trouble, so what the colony lacks now it may not be able to buy.
[lowtech] Healroot grown and dried before a fever is worth more than any amount bought after.
Help given to a people in a bad year is remembered long after it ends.

ColonyCouncil.AdvisorSignalDef.label: the camp waiting on an answer

tips.li: A camp's question left unanswered until its time runs out gets the default answer, whether or not it's the one the council would have chosen.
How the colony answers a camp is remembered when they leave, and by their people.

ColonyCouncil.AdvisorSignalDef.label: a decree that costs more than it gives

tips.li: A decree is worth its moods when what it does matters more than how people feel about it: rationing in a hungry winter, a curfew in a bad week.
A decree enacted again soon after the last time wears thinner, and the bad moods about it grow.
Who loves and who hates a decree shows on its card on the Decrees page, before it's enacted.
Offices are filled at the yearly election, or by the council from the Decrees page at any time. Overruling the colony's vote costs some trust.
Only someone who can do an office's work can hold it: nobody incapable of medicine is ever the physician.
An office helps the colony as a whole while it's filled, as well as the one who holds it.

ColonyCouncil.AdvisorSignalDef.label: a calendar day with nothing laid by

tips.li: A feast day is a meal from the stores eaten together: with no meals in store, there's nothing to sit down to.
A day of the hunt marks game for the colony's hunters, and a hunter without a bow or a gun can't take part.
A bonfire is laid from the colony's wood when it has no campfire to gather round.
A day the colony can't keep this year can be let pass, or kept another way, from the Calendar page.
A promise broken hurts more than a wish refused: it costs trust, and the one who asked remembers it for a long while.
If it can't be done in time, saying so honestly before it runs out costs less than letting it lapse.
Wood, cloth, leather and tools left out in the weather lose their condition day by day. A roof stops it.
A roof needs no walls, only something to hold it up within six cells: a few columns over a stockpile will do.
[lowtech] A storehouse of wood and straw is cheap. Keep a torch or fire out of it, or keep it clear of the houses.
Meat and vegetables rot in the warm whatever is over them; a roof only keeps the weather off.

ColonyCouncil.AdvisorSignalDef.label: food that won't keep through winter

tips.li: Pemmican keeps for months and needs only meat and vegetables, at a campfire or a stove.
Meat keeps only days in the warm. A winter mild enough to grow nothing is usually too mild to freeze it either.
Rice, corn and potatoes keep for a month or more on their own; berries and meat don't.
A campfire left lit burns about ten logs a day; torches burn wood too, more slowly.
Trees cut in summer, before the snow, are the cheapest firewood there is. Mark a stand of them for cutting.
A fire that runs out at night leaves everyone sleeping in the cold, and some of them ill by morning.
A doctor who tends their own wounds does it worse, and can't at all while unconscious.
Doctoring at a low priority is enough for a second doctor: they step in when the first is hurt or away.
Medicine skill grows fastest with practice on real patients; a second doctor learns on the small cuts and colds.
Anyone awake in the dark loses a little mood for it, and a bedroom is where people are awake in the dark most: late at night and early in the morning.
A lamp on the wall takes no floor space, which matters most in a small bedroom.
[lowtech] A wall torch lights a small room well; keep it away from anything that burns easily.
The planned lamps go where they light what is dark now, never beside the door.
Colonists eat where they are when the nearest free seat is too far away, and lose mood for it.
A small table and two chairs by the fields or the workshops saves the walk at lunch.
Packed meals carried in a pocket are eaten wherever hunger strikes; a table nearby keeps them from eating on the floor.
